content: Elliptocytosis 1, also referred to as EPB41, is a gene found in humans. This condition, elliptocytosis, is a hematologic disorder that is characterized by the presence of abnormally elliptical-shaped red blood cells (erythrocytes) and varying degrees of hemolytic anemia, which is the destruction of red blood cells leading to anemia. Elliptocytosis is inherited in an autosomal dominant manner, meaning that a single copy of the mutated gene from one parent is sufficient to cause the disorder. The condition arises due to mutations in one of several genes that encode proteins critical to the structural integrity of the red blood cell membrane skeleton. Forms of elliptocytosis that are not linked to the Rh blood group system (Rh-unlinked) are caused by mutations in specific genes, including the alpha-spectrin gene (MIM 182860), the beta-spectrin gene (MIM 182870), or the band 3 gene (MIM 109270). The EPB41 protein itself is associated with the cytoskeleton of red blood cells, playing a crucial role in maintaining their shape and mechanical stability.
